content: The drug telotristat ethyl interacts with various medications by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly through the induction of CYP3A4 and, in some cases, CYP2B6 or CYP2E1. These interactions can lead to either increased or decreased drug levels and effects, necessitating careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or the use of alternative therapies. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions and associated recommendations: 1. Diazepam (Intranasal): Co-administration with telotristat ethyl may alter diazepam elimination, either increasing or decreasing its levels. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Dihydroergotamine: Telotristat ethyl reduces dihydroergotamine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 3. Disopyramide: Similar to dihydroergotamine, telotristat ethyl decreases disopyramide levels via CYP3A4 induction. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 4. Doravirine: Co-administration is contraindicated as telotristat ethyl significantly reduces doravirine levels, potentially leading to virologic failure and resistance. 5. Efavirenz: Telotristat ethyl decreases efavirenz levels through CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider increasing the efavirenz dose if necessary. 6. Elacestrant: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces elacestrant levels via CYP3A4 induction. 7. Erdafitinib: Telotristat ethyl decreases erdafitinib levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, adjust the erdafitinib dose based on serum phosphate levels and monitor closely. 8. Ergotamine: Telotristat ethyl reduces ergotamine levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 9. Ethosuximide: Telotristat ethyl decreases ethosuximide levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 10. Everolimus: Telotristat ethyl reduces everolimus levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 11. Fedratinib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces fedratinib levels. The interaction with moderate CYP3A4 inducers has not been studied. 12. Fentanyl: Telotristat ethyl decreases fentanyl levels, potentially reducing efficacy and causing withdrawal in dependent patients. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 13. Fineranone: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces fineranone levels via CYP2E1 metabolism. 14. Fruquintinib: Telotristat ethyl increases fruquintinib levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, continue fruquintinib at the recommended dose and monitor closely. 15. Infigratinib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces infigratinib levels. 16. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Telotristat ethyl decreases isavuconazonium sulfate levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Lefamulin: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces lefamulin levels. Monitor for reduced efficacy if co-administration is unavoidable. 18. Lemborexant: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces lemborexant levels. 19. Lenacapavir: Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers, as telotristat ethyl reduces lenacapavir levels. 20. Lenolisib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces lenolisib levels. 21. Levamlodipine: Telotristat ethyl decreases levamlodipine levels. 22. Lonafarnib: Co-administration is contraindicated, as telotristat ethyl reduces lonafarnib levels. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 23. Lorlatinib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces lorlatinib levels. If unavoidable, monitor liver function tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin). 24. Lurbinectedin: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces lurbinectedin levels. 25. Mavacamten: Co-administration is contraindicated, as telotristat ethyl reduces mavacamten levels. 26. Midazolam: Telotristat ethyl decreases midazolam levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 27. Naldemedine: Telotristat ethyl reduces naldemedine levels. 28. Nirogacestat: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces nirogacestat levels. 29. Norgestrel: Telotristat ethyl reduces norgestrel levels. Consider additional barrier contraceptive methods and monitor closely. 30. Octreotide: Octreotide decreases telotristat ethyl levels. Administer short-acting octreotide at least 30 minutes after telotristat ethyl. 31. Olutasidenib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces olutasidenib levels. 32. Omaflexolone: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces omaflexolone levels. 33. Palovarotene: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces palovarotene levels. 34. Pimavanserin: Telotristat ethyl reduces pimavanserin levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 35. Pirtobrutinib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, increase the pirtobrutinib dose as recommended. 36. Praziquantel: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces praziquantel levels. 37. Pretomanid: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces pretomanid levels. Pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate. 38. Quinidine: Telotristat ethyl reduces quinidine levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 39. Quinine: Telotristat ethyl reduces quinine levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 40. Quizartinib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces quizartinib levels. 41. Repotrectinib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces repotrectinib levels. 42. Rimegepant: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces rimegepant levels. 43. Ripretinib: Telotristat ethyl reduces ripretinib levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, increase the dosing frequency and monitor closely. 44. Selumetinib: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces selumetinib levels. 45. Siponimod: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces siponimod levels. Co-administration with moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 46. Sirolimus: Telotristat ethyl reduces sirolimus levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 47. Stiripentol: Telotristat ethyl reduces stiripentol levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Sufentanil: Telotristat ethyl reduces sufentanil levels, potentially causing withdrawal in dependent patients. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 49. Tacrolimus: Telotristat ethyl reduces tacrolimus levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 50. Tazemetostat: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces tazemetostat levels. 51. Theophylline: Telotristat ethyl reduces theophylline levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 52. Tinidazole: Telotristat ethyl reduces tinidazole levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Tivozanib: Telotristat ethyl reduces tivozanib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Triazolam: Telotristat ethyl reduces triazolam levels. Therapy should be modified, and efficacy monitored closely. 55. Ubrogepant: Telotristat ethyl reduces ubrogepant levels. Dose adjustments are recommended during co-administration. 56. Voclosporin: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces voclosporin levels. 57. Zuranolone: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as telotristat ethyl reduces zuranolone levels. Adverse Effects: Common side effects include nausea (13%), headache (11%), increased GGT (9%), depression (9%), peripheral edema (7%), flatulence (7%), decreased appetite (7%), fever (7%), abdominal pain (5%), and constipation (5%). Less common effects include increased alkaline phosphatase, ALT, and AST levels, as well as intestinal obstruction, angioedema, pruritus, and rash. Warnings: Telotristat ethyl may reduce bowel movement frequency, potentially leading to severe constipation and abdominal pain. Patients should be monitored for these symptoms, and the drug should be discontinued if severe complications develop. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: There is no human data on the use of telotristat ethyl during pregnancy. It is unknown if the drug is excreted in breast milk. The benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and potential adverse effects on the infant. Administration: Telotristat ethyl should be taken with food. When used with short-acting octreotide, administer octreotide at least 30 minutes after telotristat ethyl. Storage: Store at controlled room temperature (25°C or 77°F), with excursions permitted between 15-30°C (59-86°F).
